questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz$,  find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,-1,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,-1,-1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz)\text{ }k \\  & =(2xy-z)\text{ }i+({x}^{2}+2y)\text{ }j-xk \\ ∇\,f(2,-1,-1) & =(\,2(2)(-1)-(-1)\,)\text{ }i+(\,{2}^{2}+2(-1)\,)\text{ }j-2k \\  & =-3\,i+2\,j-2\,k \\  & =⟨-3,2,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,-1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-3,2,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z+1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }k \\  & =2y{e}^{x}\text{ }i+2{e}^{x}\text{ }j-{e}^{z}k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,-1) & =2(1)e\text{ }i+2e\text{ }j-{e}^{-1}k \\  & =2e\,i+2e\,j-{e}^{-1}k \\  & =⟨2e,2e,-\frac{1}{e}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2e,2e,-\frac{1}{e}⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ 2ex+2ey-\frac{z}{e}-4e-\frac{1}{e} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=xyz-{z}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,3,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,3,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz-{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz-{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz-{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+(xy-2z)k \\ ∇\,f(2,3,1) & =(3)(1)\text{ }i+2(1)\text{ }j+(2(3)-2(1))k \\  & =3\,i+2\,j+4k \\  & =⟨3,2,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,3,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨3,2,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 3(x-2)+2(y-3)+4(z-1) & =0 \\ 3x+2y+4z-16 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface ${e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}=e-3.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,-1),$ what is the value of $\frac{a-b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)={e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=e-3.$  

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2})i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2})k \\  & =(y{e}^{xy}-2x)i+(x{e}^{xy})j+(-4z)k \\ ∇f(1,1,-1) & =((1){e}^{(1)(1)}-2(1))\text{ }i+(1){e}^{(1)(1)}\text{ }j+(-4)(-1)\text{ }k \\  & =(e-2)\text{ }i+e\text{ }j+4\text{ }k \\  & =⟨e-2,\,e,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨e-2,\,e,\,4⟩.$

Finally, $\frac{a-b}{c}=\frac{(e-2)-e}{4}=-\frac{1}{2}.$

questions.problem: Consider the surface ${z}^{2}y+16=4\sqrt{x}+y.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(4,-1,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}y+16 & =4\sqrt{x}+y. \\ {z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)={z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-16.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(4,-1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y)\text{ }k \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}\text{ }i+({z}^{2}-1)\text{ }j+2zy\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(4,-1,3) & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{4}}\text{ }i+({3}^{2}-1)\text{ }j+2(3)(-1)\text{ }k \\  & =-\,i+8\text{ }j-6\,k \\  & =⟨-1,8,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(4,-1,3)\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y+1,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,8,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y+1,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ -(x-4)+8(y+1)-6(z-3) & =0 \\ -x+8y-6z+30 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
